label: neiso 40 oil budget
definition: (PROBE — REJECTED) neiso-40 = neiso-39 keeper recipe + neiso_oil_burn_budget flag ON: adds an inventory-limited monthly oil-burn LP constraint (one row per oil-primary generator × month, upper bound = EIA-923 Schedule 5 petroleum receipts converted to MWh). Goal: produce >$300 scarcity-tail hours (C3c) by endogenously pricing marginal oil MWh when the monthly budget binds in cold-snap months. NULL FINDING: F923 petroleum receipt coverage is too sparse to support the constraint — only 1-2 NEISO plants report petroleum receipts (out of 140 oil-primary generators / 5345 MW), and in 2025 only 2/12 months have any deliveries. A sparsity guard (requires ≥6 months with deliveries AND ≥5% of fleet reporting) correctly skips the constraint in all 3 years, producing a solve identical to neiso-39. The fundamental issue: F923 receipts measure fuel deliveries to tank, not inventory available to burn — zero receipts in a month doesn't mean zero oil available (plants burn from stored inventory). Dual-fuel gas units (6831 MW) are excluded from the constraint because their oil consumption isn't captured in F923 petroleum receipts (they report as gas plants). The C3c scarcity tail requires a different mechanism — likely a forward-derivable winter fuel-inventory or delivery-logistics constraint, not monthly F923 receipts.
